They read the code before asking for help. They picked up new tools without being told to. They weren't thrown by systems they didn't understand on day one. And they built things that held up in production.

**That's who we're looking for.**

**The opportunity**

Peri is recruiting Software Engineers, including founding and early backend roles, for some of New York's most compelling AI startups, from Seed to Series D+, backed by investors including a16z, Sequoia Capital, Founders Fund, Notable Capital, and Thrive.

We've worked closely with the founders, studied the engineers who thrive on their teams, and learned what really sets them apart.

The short version:
**ownership, speed, technical judgment, and the ability to learn fast often count for more than the name at the top of your last offer letter.**

**You don't need to have worked on AI products already. If you have, great. If you haven't, keep reading.**

**What you'll actually do**

Imagine joining a team where the product is still taking shape.

There's no thick onboarding doc. The architecture has decisions you'd make differently. The roadmap changes when a customer says something surprising.

Your job is to make it work. Understand what users actually need. Make the tradeoffs. Design the system, write the code, ship it, and fix it when real traffic finds what tests didn't.

**You're part builder, part architect, part problem-solver.**

You'll work directly with founders. You'll own features and systems end to end, not just tickets. And you'll see your work in front of customers within days, not quarters.

These roles are for engineers who like having the whole problem.

**Who we're looking for**

Maybe you're an engineer at a big company who keeps wanting to touch more of the stack than your team allows.

Maybe you taught yourself, switched careers, or grew into responsibilities long before anyone gave you the title for them.

**We take all of that seriously.**
But here's the thing.
**We need you to show us.**

A resume won't tell us how you debug something you've never seen, how you make decisions with incomplete information, or what you do when the obvious approach falls over.

So walk us through it.

Tell us about a system you designed. A bug that took you days to track down. A technology you had to master in a week. Something you built that nobody asked you to build.

It doesn't need to be impressive-sounding. It needs to be real.

**Why aren't the companies listed?**

Because this isn't one opening. We work with several teams looking for similar engineers, each building something different.

Rather than you running six interview loops in parallel, we'd like to understand how you think and what you're great at, then point you toward the teams where you'd fit best.

**We only work with companies we'd be excited to join ourselves.**

**Who is Peri?**

Most technical recruiting is keyword matching: languages, frameworks, years of experience, last employer.

We think that leaves a lot of great engineers on the table.

So we start from the other end. We learn from founders what actually makes an engineer succeed on their team, then look for those qualities in people whose resumes may undersell them.

We're most interested in engineers who are better than their credentials suggest.

* Apply through the link and DM me on LinkedIn.
* We do want one answer:
  **What's the hardest or most interesting thing you've built, and what about it makes you think you're capable of more than your resume shows?**
* A few sentences is enough. A link to code or a project is even better. Specifics beat buzzwords.
* If there's a fit, we'll talk, share what we know about each team, and help you figure out which roles make sense. When there's a strong match, we'll connect you directly with the founders.

**And if you've ever thought, "I'm a much better engineer than my resume makes me look," we especially want to hear from you.**

**One last thing**

Looking past credentials doesn't mean looking past ability.

If you're mass-applying without reading the post, can't show real engineering work, have a fabricated or misleading LinkedIn profile, or aren't authorized to work in the United States, please don't apply.

**It's not a good use of anyone's time.**
We'll overlook a pedigree. We won't overlook a lack of effort, skill, or honesty.

**Show us what you've shipped, not what you say you can ship.**
